description:
We are a Cairo-based team of university students participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We are working on the "Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map" challenge, aiming to develop an interactive Mars exploration platform using NASA's open scientific data.

Our interests include software development, artificial intelligence, data analysis, geospatial visualization, and space exploration.
summary:
Red Planet Lab is an intelligent Mars exploration decision-support platform that fuses multi-mission orbital and in-situ planetary datasets into an interactive 3D environment for autonomous rover traverse planning.

Addressing the challenge of navigating hazardous extraterrestrial terrain, we developed a system that harmonizes NASA MOLA topographic elevation models, Viking orbital imagery, USGS geologic stratigraphic maps, and real in-situ atmospheric telemetry from Perseverance (MEDA) and Curiosity (REMS). Users can explore any sector on a 3D Martian globe, reconstruct 3D surface meshes, and run a physics-constrained A∗ routing engine that evaluates three strategies: Fastest, Safest (which actively detects and bypasses dynamic dust storms and slope hazards), and Scientific Exploration (maximizing scientific ROI across geologic outcrops).

Crucially, traverses are benchmarked against historical NASA rover paths and verified with in-situ surface photography. Red Planet Lab bridges the gap between raw planetary data and explainable mission operations, reducing rover risk, safeguarding payloads, and accelerating scientific discovery on Mars.
